content: Dinoprostone, commonly known by the brand name Cervidil, is a medication used to prepare the cervix (the lower opening of the uterus) for labor and delivery. It is typically administered to women with a normal pregnancy who are at or near their delivery due date. Dinoprostone is a naturally occurring substance in the body that helps prepare for labor. This medication is inserted high in the vagina, near the cervix, by a healthcare professional. During the procedure, the patient will lie down, and it is usually necessary to remain lying down for two hours after the insertion. Dinoprostone should only be used in a hospital setting where trained medical care is available. Patients will be closely monitored for changes in the cervix, signs of active labor (such as the breaking of water or strong, sustained contractions), and the condition of the baby. The healthcare provider will remove the insert if side effects occur, after 12 hours, or when it is no longer needed. Side effects of dinoprostone are uncommon and generally mild, including fever, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or abdominal pain. Rarely, this medication can cause uterine rupture, a serious condition that may require emergency surgery. Symptoms of uterine rupture include severe pain in the uterus and an abnormal heart rate in the baby. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are also rare but can occur. If a hypersensitivity reaction is suspected, the medication should be removed, and appropriate supportive therapy should be initiated. Precautions should be taken before using dinoprostone. Patients should inform their doctor, midwife, or pharmacist if they are allergic to this medication or have any other allergies. The product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other problems. During pregnancy, dinoprostone should only be used when clearly needed. It is unknown if this drug passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter the effectiveness of dinoprostone or increase the risk of serious side effects. Patients should keep a list of all medications and products they use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal supplements, and share it with their healthcare provider. In the event of an overdose, which can be harmful if swallowed, immediate medical attention is required. If someone experiences severe symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call emergency services (911 in the U.S.). Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222 for assistance. This medication should not be flushed down the toilet or poured into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard the product when it is expired or no longer needed. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this medication and your specific health needs.
